newsitem.title: UK: UN says Iraq on track to hit $1bn oil export target.
newsitem.headline: UN says Iraq on track to hit $1bn oil export target.

text.p: The United Nations said on Wednesday Iraqi crude exports under an oil-for-food deal implemented last December were on track to raise $1 billion during the first 90 days.
"It's my guess it will be close to $1 billion by the time we get into March," said Fred Eckhard, spokesman for U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Since early February, when U.N. overseers put the total value of the first three month's contracts at about $800 million, the United Nations has approved Iraq's requests to sell extra crude on the spot market to compensate for falling world oil prices.
Six new contracts totalling 6.05 million barrels have been approved, taking the total number of contracts to 33. Another two contracts were being considered, U.N. sources said on Tuesday.

Under the terms of the deal, Iraq is permitted to sell $1 billion worth of crude from December 10 to March 9, and then another $1 billion for the next 90 days to pay for food and humanitarian supplies distributed under strict U.N. supervision.
U.N. sanctions imposed after Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990 remain in force.

In a preliminary report issued on Tuesday, the U.N. said as of February 21 the balance in the escrow account holding oil receipts stood at $482 million. An additional $112 million was expected from February 21-28, putting the total at $594 million.
The revenue in the account is not expected to reach $1 billion until early April because of deferred payments for oil already exported in the first three-month period.
"This ($594 million) is the amount that has already been paid," said an official at Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation by telephone from Baghdad.
SOMO's customers do not have to pay for the oil they receive until 30 days after the bill of lading has been issued on completion of loading.
Revenue is expected to flow into the account at a rate of about $12 million a day.
Eckhard said the U.N. Secretary General still believed the plan would be renewed for another six months when it expires in June.
"He feels there will be an extension," he said.
-- Mark Thompson, Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
